newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource sees big savings from network merger.
newsitem.headline: Unisource sees big savings from network merger.

text.p: European telecommunications joint venture Unisource said on Wednesday its agreement to merge the international networks of its partners would deliver cost savings of up to 30 percent.

Unisource, which groups the telecom arm of Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT, said it was tightening its alliance by bringing together the individual networks into Unisource Carrier Service UCS from 1998.
"By doing this there will be rationalisation benefits, the cost level will go down 20-30 percent," Unisource president and chief executive Paul Smits said in a telephone interview.

Smits said the merger move would produce a company with initial revenues of $2.0 billion a year and around 900 employees. "The existing UCS deals with an operation of around 200 people," he said, not giving existing UCS revenues.
The combination of networks would mean the existing UCS network, essentially a wholesale telecoms carrier at the moment, would become much denser, said Smits.

"That will allow a striking rationalisation because from that moment this European network will be managed from one point, so double switches, double connections, double network management centres will be very quickly dealt with," he said.
Smits said Unisource could also attract more business as it slashed back its own overheads and offered tariffs to customers that more closely reflected industry costs.
"The most important thing is that in the new telecoms arena this big wholesale company will offer true cost-oriented tariffs...which will accelerate usage and allow further growth," said Smits.

"The overriding thing is that in the new arena it's everything to do with being competitive, having large volumes, extremely slim organisations, dealing with the newest technology, offering extremely low tariffs," he said. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
